Using one and one and a half years of LHC data collected by the LHCb experiment, we have analyzed the $B^0_S\rightarrowK^+K^-$ decay to determine the $B^0_S$ lifespan. By examining time-dependent CP asymmetries in this decay, we estimated effective lifetimes for both light quark components, denoted as $\beta$ and $\alpha$, of $B^0_S$ mesons. Additionally, we calculated the actual $B^0_S$ meson lifespan as well as for these two components. The results we obtained are $t_{\rel}^{\rel}(\alpha)=0.839\pm 0.033\pm 0.014\pm 0.011$ ps, $t_{\rel}^{\rel}(\beta)=0.841\pm 0.033\pm 0.014\pm 0.011$ ps, $\tau_{B^0_S}=1.453\pm 0.054\pm 0.024\pm 0.018$ ps, where the first uncertainties stem from the data, the second from simulation, and the third from external sources.

A numerical method is proposed to solve the discretized control problem with a random evolution operator. Our approach involves approximating the random operator using a Lévy chain, which enables us to calculate the probability of control dissemination within a network. Our numerical method is demonstrated through simulations of the probability of disseminating information, and it shows that our approach yields more precise results than an existing numerical method.

At the extreme energy end of the spectrum, the origin of cosmic rays becomes elusive, and the detection of their anisotropic patterns from the sky can offer vital clues. Researchers at the Pierre Auger Observatory analyzed the directional distribution of 11,007 high-energy cosmic-ray events with energies exceeding 4 EeV recorded between 2004 and 2017. By comparing the anisotropic patterns across different time periods, they found a correlation with the Large Magellanic Cloud's apparent position in the sky. Moreover, the degree of alignment with this pattern varied across different years, and its significance was found to be directly related to the duration of observation. Furthermore, the study revealed that smaller time-scale variations in anisotropy exhibited characteristics of rotationally symmetric patterns around the axis of the Earth's axis.

This research paper proves that Zinbiel algebras are completely solvable, providing a Zinbiel version to a previously established fact for Lie algebras. Additionally, it demonstrates that free Lie algebras cannot be represented as faithful quotients of Lie-assocative algebras, whereas they can be represented as faithful quotients of Zinbiel algebras.

This research investigates the behavior of directed flow in lead-lead collisions at the LHC, specifically at a total center-of-mass energy of 5.02 TeV. By utilizing the flow vector, variations in flow direction and intensity are studied across different collision centrality levels and particle transverse momentum. The findings reveal that 3-4 degrees fluctuations in angle occur at low transverse momentum, gradually decreasing to 2 degrees at higher transverse momentum. Moreover, the data indicates that directed flow rises linearly with mid-rapidity for both mid-central and central collisions. The results obtained in this study are compared with previous results from lead-lead collisions at a higher energy level of 2.76 TeV.

This research focuses on resolving differences in tables that have missing data entries. Initially, we outline various types of discrepancies that can occur. Subsequently, we examine a particular category of discrepancies, known as functional discrepancies, and develop a specific technique to address them. This technique involves creating and using a type of graphical representation called a global dependency graph. We implement this technique and compare its performance against an existing method, which is widely used and accounts for missing data entries. Through these experiments, we find that our method, referred to as NullPar, consistently produces more accurate results than the existing technique. Additionally, we make our code publicly available on GitHub.

Linear Poisson regression models are commonly used to forecast future values based on past data.  However, the effectiveness of these models in predicting time-series data with varying seasonal patterns or trends is limited.  In this work, we introduce a novel model called the temporal varying Poisson autoregressive model, which extends the applicability of linear Poisson regression models to a broader range of scenarios.  This new model enables more accurate predictions of future values by incorporating its unique parameters.  We evaluate the model's performance through simulations and apply it to real-world data to demonstrate its effectiveness.

Object representation is crucial for 3D understanding, yet conventional approaches mainly focus on generalizing from existing data. Current methods, such as point clouds, voxel grids, and polygon meshes, often struggle with limited scene understanding and generalization capabilities. In this work, we introduce Neural Description Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation that is voxel-based, compact, and capable of capturing complex shape relationships. NDFs are point-set equivalent and achieve an unprecedented state-of-the-art performance of over 20 points in adapting to new categories in zero-shot and few-shot settings on the ShapeNet dataset. To further enhance its applicability, we make the NDF code publicly available.

A universal length scale characterizes traditional universality categories defined by the same order parameter and symmetries, independent of system size. While most universality classes have multiple representations, five established Yang-Lee universality classes with distinct representations exist, yet their positional relationship remains unclear. This study provides accurate estimates of Yang-Lee edge criticality for five representation classes in traditional O(N) universality frameworks, including a novel, thorough examination of the 24 representation class of O(4) universality. Precise representations for O(2), O(3), and O(4) are positively identified for the first time. Through a comprehensive comparison of representation scale ratios across susceptibility and structure factor, this work establishes reliable benchmarks for future research.

In statistics and machine learning, basic convex optimization often fails to explain the effective non-convex optimization methods that work so well in high-dimensional settings. As an example of this, we examine the teacher-student perceptron model and show there's a way to reframe its learning process as largely non-convex, except for a small part. Building on this perspective, we achieve two non-convex optimization results. Firstly, we prove the majority of the teacher perceptron's learning landscape is strictly non-convex. Specifically, we show that within a key region of learning loss values, the average over multiple learning objectives is provably non-convex, with a significant part (over 99.999...%) of this region showing local optimality equivalent to zero loss. This approach offers an alternative to the earlier, more technical proof provided by Ben Arous and Berthet. Moreover, we demonstrate that a random transformation of the features can make this approach applicable, allowing us to conclude that the average free energy of the Hopfield model is largely non-convex after this transformation.

Recent research has revisited using basic photometric data from traditional astronomy to quantify atmospheric aerosols. By reanalyzing point source photometry from nearly two decades of Britain's John Innes Centre Variable Star Observers measurements, we identified significant delays in periodic stars with well-documented periods, indicating they are not artifacts of the study. By comparing the photometric data of periodic stars before and after a known supernova event, we successfully reconstructed the 1986A supernova's light curve in multiple color bands, even in remote observations. However, using variable star photometry to determine aerosols presents several challenges, including revising standard analysis methods, accounting for host galaxy contributions, and mitigating the impact of light pollution and scintillation. By studying the variable star region 508 and re-examining historical observations, we found evidence of significant changes in variable star region 508 that point to light pollution rather than scintillation. By re-examining the HST photometric data of the RR Lyrae star BL Her, we demonstrated that even precise space-based observations require careful interpretation. By re-interpreting the light curve data of the galaxy NGC 5585 using the V754 Pic, we found that space-based observations can also introduce significant delays in periodic stars. By re-analyzing the photometric data of the galaxy NGC 5585 with different filters, we estimated an unusually high aerosol optical depth

To accurately estimate the complete six-degree-of-freedom pose of objects within unstructured environments, robust object pose determination methods are essential. To address the limitations of existing techniques, we introduce a novel approach called DeepHMap++, building upon the foundational deep hue map concept. This approach incorporates two key enhancements: first, a clustering algorithm is applied to combine hue channels into a compact five-channel projection, and second, a correspondence learning module is added to the projection cluster head, enabling the model to learn semantic features and refine pose estimation. The DP-CC head is a key differentiator of our approach, setting it apart from existing methods. Our method is trained using a combination of cluster head and correspondence head losses. To validate the effectiveness of our approach, we conducted extensive experiments on the KITTI dataset, comparing our results with state-of-the-art methods and analyzing the contributions of each component individually. The results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing object pose determination techniques for unstructured environments.

We present GGLasso, a Python-based tool for Generalized Graphical Lasso
computation, which identifies the most concise representation of conditional
independence between variables in a set of multiple related Gaussian
covariance matrices. Employing the Newton's method, our algorithm efficiently
converges on a precise solution, which we achieve by incorporating a
Generalized Positive SemiDefinite projection. GGLasso enables researchers to
work with complex data sets, which may include seasonally relevant patterns
such as weather-related crop yields, while yielding compact and interpretable
relationships between variables that hold true across different seasons.

A molecular dynamics (MD) method known as the Langevin Dynamics (LD) has been widely utilized in recent years to predict the structural configurations of complex molecules. However, an examination of the configurations produced by LD, when compared to those generated through advanced sampling techniques like Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), reveals significant discrepancies. This study explores the underlying causes of such differences and the limitations of LD in accurately capturing the statistical properties of molecular structures. Furthermore, we explore potential enhancements to LD, including the implementation of simulated annealing and an optimization of the temperature parameter, to improve the accuracy of complex molecule structure prediction through LD-based methods.

As complex systems evolve from simple to multi-layered representations, traditional Eigenvector Prominence (EP) analysis falls short, necessitating an advanced method, Multiplex EP (MuEP), for identifying influential nodes across network layers. MuEP considers interlayer node connections and incorporates them into Eigenvector Centrality calculations, resulting in a prominence score that reflects node importance within a specific network layer and their link to related nodes in other layers. Experimental validation using both synthetic and real-world multi-layered networks demonstrates the effectiveness of MuEP, showcasing its superior performance in community detection, time-varying network analysis, and multi-layered EP anomaly detection compared to existing techniques.

In 1928, Dirac formulated his seminal equation, establishing the connection between classical relativistic mechanics and its quantum counterpart. Our research introduces a method to derive this equation directly from the classical Gauss law in R-Minkowski spacetimes. We first establish the gauge-invariant R-Schrödinger field equation, then multiply by the conjugate of the R-Dirac field and integrate over space to obtain the quantum law, which, through a straightforward manipulation, yields the R-Dirac equation. Our approach diverges from previous methods by not employing any ad-hoc substitutions. Our derived formula is analogous to the one originally presented by Dirac, although our method does not account for his initial motivation.

When a sphere moves at a moderate speed through a liquid and makes contact with a surface, it can create a temporary vacuum seal that significantly slows down the sphere's movement. This study investigates how various factors, including the sphere's speed, the surrounding fluid's viscosity, and the surface's texture, influence how long this seal lasts. By using high-speed video analysis, we measured the time the seal endures for different scenarios. Our findings show that for conditions where a seal forms, the time it persists is influenced by a combination of a sphere's speed and factors representing viscosity and surface texture. Additionally, we discovered that an increase in surface micro-structure can lead to a significant decrease in seal duration. Our data also indicates that as the sphere's speed increases, the time it takes to break the seal is directly related to its speed.

In the context of Type IIB supergravity, we investigate the possible universal symmetries that can be broken and the resulting general coupling forms of axion-dilaton fields with non-Abelian gauge fields. We then explore the Lagrangians of Type IIB 14D effective field theories, taking into account their non-universal general coupling forms of theta-terms.

Our angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements cubanite reveal significant orbital asymmetry between the Cu 3d(x2-y2) and Cu 3d(xy) bands.
Cubanite displays strong electron localization, characterized by broadened spectral features, absent collective excitations, and highly asymmetric band
broadening for the two Cu 3d orbitals.
The isotropic nature cubanite possesses results in elliptical electron
orbits for the two types of Cu 3d electrons, explaining the observed
electron asymmetry.
The elliptical nature also accounts for the absence of
collective excitations and anisotropic band broadening in cubanite.

The movement of excitons in semiconducting materials is heavily influenced by their interaction with localized charge carriers, which can significantly affect Rabi oscillations.  When performing Rabi oscillations using a pulsed laser, the frequency and phase of the rotating dark exciton state should theoretically lag behind the bright exciton state by $2\pi/q$, where $q$ is the angular momentum of the dark exciton.  However, in our study on InAs quantum dots, we observed a $2\pi/2$ phase lag between the bright and dark Rabi oscillations, even in the absence of any external torque.  By conducting frequency sweeps and simulations, we determined the Rabi frequency and phase for both bright and dark Rabi oscillations, and found that the interaction between dark excitons and charged electrons is $10$ times stronger than that between bright excitons and charged electrons, as evidenced by a $10$ times broader dressing width.  Furthermore, we observed that the frequency and phase of the Rabi oscillations are affected by the detuning angle, and that the $2\pi/2$ phase lag is a result of the quantum mechanical properties of the dark exciton.

Three-dimensional lattice structures are broadly classified into four distinct phases based on symmetry principles. Wallpaper lattices, which are two-dimensional counterparts, are divided into six categories. Notably, within each category, multiple lattice structures with varying symmetries exist. In this study, we investigate the potential to manipulate the position of Dirac points in a two-dimensional type-5 wallpaper lattice. By applying symmorphic periodic boundary conditions to a non-symmorphic hexagonal lattice under both spinless and time-reversal symmetries, we demonstrate that lattice deformation and the introduction of next-nearest-neighbor hopping can alter the position of Dirac points in a controlled manner. Building on this principle, we further explore a non-Hermitian Hombly lattice within the same non-symmorphic wallpaper category and find that the interplay of multiple symmetries in this lattice allows for the tuning of Dirac point positions in both real and imaginary momentum spaces through the adjustment of hopping parameters. These findings provide a framework for the exploration and design of novel two-dimensional lattice structures with enhanced functional properties.

Quantum superpositions of distinct classical states form the basis for powerful quantum technologies, yet they are highly susceptible to decoherence, which severely limits the potential of quantum technologies. Quantum-optical catalysis, a novel process that can be found in recent studies, utilizes short-lived single-photon particles to protect and generate unique quantum states known as single-photon facilitated coherent superpositions. Research simulations show that this catalytic process significantly enhances the production of such states while also endowing photons that create them with highly distinctive, unusual properties. Furthermore, this catalytic process can be adjusted to manage the distinct classical components of these states, thus making it an adaptable and versatile tool for the controlled production of highly distinctive quantum states.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors is an important aspect that has not been widely appreciated. We demonstrate how the Newman-Penrose framework can be connected to the Riemann-Cartan theory by introducing a set of four null basis vectors and exploring the relationship between these vectors and tetrad fields. This enables us to express the Poincaré group algebra in terms of the Clifford algebra and establish a direct correspondence between the null basis vectors and the self-dual and anti-self-dual parts of the bivector. In the context of the Riemann-Cartan theory, the complexified Newman-Penrose components of the Weyl curvature tensor are shown to have a direct relationship with the self-dual and anti-self-dual parts of the bivector, with the anti-self-dual part being related to gravitational instantons.

This research combines two methods, integer programming and generalized automata, to address the issue of deducting properties of linear polymers. Initially, we establish a technique for property deduction for linear polymers using automated theorem proving. Subsequently, we apply this technique to deduce specific properties of the M323 polymer through the Prover9 tool. Linear polymers consist of a sequence of linked molecules, where each molecule has two connection points, can be either open or closed, and may possess additional properties. We demonstrate how to formulate first-order logic axioms to deduce properties of these polymers, including the number of closed molecules, property repetition frequency, and the presence of circular formations. To tackle more intricate property deductions, we establish two more axioms that enable the deduction of properties that occur a certain number of times consecutively or in a circular formation. To address issues with this technique for certain properties, we establish two alternative sets of axioms that effectively address the shortcomings by allowing us to dedicate properties such as the absence of consecutive molecules with a specific property or in circular formations. To further address property deductions, we propose an alternative set of axioms that facilitate the deduction of the number of molecules with a specific property in linear, M323, and M333 polymers.

Segmenting neoplasms in the esophagus from computed tomography images is a difficult task due to the low contrast between the tumor and surrounding tissue, as well as the varying shape and orientation of the esophagus. Deep learning models have shown promise in image segmentation tasks, but current networks often struggle with issues such as low resolution and irregular shapes. In this work, we present a novel network called the Dilated Dense Focus Unet (DDAUnet) for esophageal neoplasm segmentation in CT images. This network combines the strengths of Unet and Dense Unet architectures, and incorporates dilated convolutions to improve feature extraction and preserve high-resolution details. We also propose a focus attention module to enhance the detection of irregular shapes and improve segmentation accuracy. To train the network, we use a combination of Dice loss and Dice weighted pixel-wise cross entropy loss functions. Our approach is evaluated on two publicly available datasets, and shows promise in terms of performance.

Multilingualism is an issue that many people around the world grapple with on a daily basis. Despite the availability of monolingual resources and technologies, a lack of specialized, single-language materials hinders the development of effective tools for multilingual communities. This study aims to address this gap by focusing on code-switching and influencing factors in multilingualism. Previous research has primarily examined code-switching in the context of adjacent sentence phenomena, whereas this study takes a more in-depth approach by investigating factors that lead to code-mixing within the same sentence. A new dataset has been created to facilitate this research, consisting of over 10,000 Tagalog-English mixed sentences along with annotations for identified obstacle words and mixing influencing factors. A unique dtw-based algorithm has been used to code-switch sentences, whereas standard annotators have verified the results. This study also explores the effectiveness of existing machine translation models in handling code-switching, as well as the development of a custom ensemble model using sequence labelling techniques. The outcomes of this research and the associated dataset are publicly accessible to support future code-mixing research.

Utilizing human feedback to improve image description generation has been a key research area for several platforms, including Amazon, Microsoft, and Google. This paper investigates the effectiveness of human references in enhancing evaluation methods for image descriptions, evaluating three evaluation approaches: standard metrics, assisted evaluation with references, and evaluation using descriptions from peer images. Our study involves a large-scale assessment conducted on six distinct datasets representing various image generators. The results indicate that employing human reference images can lead to more accurate evaluation measurements that better reflect user satisfaction, particularly when using image descriptions from peer images as the assessment method outperforms others. Furthermore, this approach is especially well-suited for large-scale evaluations, making it a practical and efficient alternative to traditional, time-consuming methods.

Tantalum pentoxide, commonly referred to as Ta$_2$O$_5$, is a key component in numerous applications, including optical coatings, capacitors, and semiconductors. Its complex structure, consisting of multiple crystalline forms, contributes to its diverse properties. Despite extensive research into its composition, the underlying crystal structure remains elusive. In this work, ten distinct Ta$_2$O$_5$ crystal configurations are investigated, encompassing previously unexplored configurations. By employing density functional theory, the research reveals that phase A exhibits the lowest energy state among all configurations. However, the B-phase demonstrates the lowest macroscopic elastic energy, which is a critical factor in determining the stable configuration on a macroscopic scale. To further investigate the likelihood of each configuration existing in nature, the research utilizes the Grand Canonical Monte Carlo method to simulate crystal growth. The results reveal that the B-phase has the highest probability of occurrence in nature, followed by phase A. The effectiveness of geographic misinformation was examined in this study among 480 Reddit users in the United States. It investigated how inaccurate maps depicting country borders and major city locations impacted their ability to identify erroneous geographic information. The results revealed that users struggled to detect incorrect maps of large countries but excelled at spotting errors in smaller countries and city locations. The study explored the potential implications of Big Geographic Arrangements on misinformation and offered explanations for its effects. It was discussed how this type of misinformation could be utilized to distort perceptions of a country's size and influence, as well as its limitations and potential applications. The findings were put into perspective by analyzing comparable studies on misinformation and presenting related studies on cognitive biases and mental models. The study called for the creation of more accurate mental models of smaller countries and locations to prevent misinformation and enhance public understanding.

Verbal guidance from humans is a key component for effective robotic learning through demonstration. Yet, it remains unclear what verbal instructions are necessary for robots to successfully learn from humans. This study focuses on equipping a robot with the right acoustic tools to process verbal demonstration information. We investigated human instructors' speech patterns when teaching a robot a task by means of spoken language. Specifically, we analyzed speech data from instructors explaining task sequences to a robot, comparing it to speech data from the same instructors explaining the same sequences to another person. Our findings revealed that the content of speech remains consistent across both scenarios, but the acoustic patterns differ significantly. Human instructions exhibited a higher degree of temporal structure in their speech, which is essential for a robot to effectively process and interpret the information. Our results provide valuable insights for developing acoustic tools that enable robots to process the temporally structured information conveyed through speech.

The primary objective of this research is to establish a connection between field theory concepts and the Euler-Arnold equations, which describe the dynamics of a rigid body. To achieve this, we first examine how the co-jet bundle of a configuration space can be used to define field theory variables in both straightforward and complex scenarios. To illustrate the latter, we make use of the Carnot-Caratheodory metric on the Heisenberg group. Subsequently, we explore the relationship between the variational sequence of the hefted 1-form representing a path's moment arm and a rigid body's equations of motion. To illustrate the intricate nature of this connection in complex scenarios, the variational sequence is expressed in the geometric language of the co-jet bundle of a 1-form.

Conversational systems are being used in conversations with humans in various contexts, and their effectiveness is being measured using subjective user experience assessment methods. This study introduces an automated evaluation method that supplements user experience assessment by utilizing subjective ratings from users to create reference responses, which are then used to evaluate interactions between bots and users through automated evaluation techniques. This approach ensures that automated evaluation frameworks are aligned with what users rate highly.

Recently, recommendation systems have turned to aspect-based preferences for their effectiveness in capturing complex human desires and addressing diverse multi-task recommendation challenges. However, existing approaches primarily treat multi-task aspect-based recommendations in single-domain settings, neglecting the potential of cross-domain knowledge to enhance performance. This study introduces a novel Multi-Sparse-Domain Cooperative Recommendation framework, ABPM, which combines through-put learning to capture the richness of aspect preferences and a poly-matrix decomposition model to share sparse knowledge across different domains. The results of the ABPM approach demonstrate superior performance compared to existing methods in multi-sparse-d aspect recommendations.

Recent breakthroughs in optimization have introduced convex optimization as a third approach, supplementing traditional linear programming and mathematical decomposition methods for tackling large-scale organic problems. Our research introduces Hypatia, a Julia-based platform that automates the creation of convex problem formulations by analyzing source code, utilizing DataDependenceGraphs to identify variable relationships and generate comprehensive graph models. This model facilitates the extraction of problem characteristics, including linearity, non-linearity, and non-convexity, which can then be transformed into a convex formulation through the application of graph theory and optimization reformulation techniques. Our proposed hypervisualization of this process and an automated end-product are showcased, showcasing Hypatia's ability to produce a convex version of an organic recommendation algorithm.

Medical imaging is crucial in diagnosing and treating various conditions, yet image quality assurance remains a significant challenge. Deep learning has been shown to effectively predict image quality, outperforming traditional methods. However, these models often fail to generalize to new cases due to their tendency to memorize data. In this study, we investigate the issue of memorization in this context and develop a novel transfer learning framework that improves model performance while reducing overfitting. Our framework yields more robust results than standard transfer learning approaches and achieves greater efficiency in computation.

During extreme weather events, power grid failures can lead to prolonged outages for large numbers of people. Resilience, the ability to recover quickly, is a key aspect of managing this risk. Private electric vehicles have the potential to aid recovery efforts by providing temporary power to essential services through their onboard batteries. However, coordinating a vast number of private users can be a complex task. This paper introduces a novel market design that leverages privately held EVs to boost grid resilience, along with a new multi-agent optimization algorithm to effectively match user demands with available resources. The model and algorithm are demonstrated through numerical simulations, showcasing their ability to address real-world challenges.

In this paper, we tackle a challenging multi-agent problem known as multi-agent recurrent meeting, where multiple self-interested vehicles must meet within a specific time frame to exchange information. We first establish a game theory model for meeting two opposing vehicles, and then extend this to a recurrent scenario involving the meeting of multiple vehicles. We analyze our models to determine the conditions under which a successful meeting is guaranteed and the optimal meeting point to minimize waiting time. Moreover, we propose a novel incentive mechanism to encourage cooperative behavior and avoid unnecessary delays. To test the effectiveness of our approach, we conduct extensive simulations that examine the relationship between the drive-based incentive and the cost of recurrent meeting.

This paper delves into the structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of GdSn$_3$, CmSn$_3$, and a series of Gd$_x$Cm$_{1-x}$Sn$_3$ compounds with varying Gd concentrations. Using a full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method within the framework of density functional theory, we found that both Gd and Cm exhibit an antiferromagnetic ground state within the R$\bar{3}$m space group structure. Our calculations revealed that GdSn$_3$ shows antiferromagnetic behavior, whereas CmSn$_3$ displays paramagnetism. Furthermore, GdSn$_3$ is predicted to be a type-II Weyl semi-metal, whereas CmSn$_3$ is a semi-metal with a very narrow band gap. The calculated magnetic moment for GdSn$_3$ is 7.0 $\mu_B$, whereas CmSn$_3$ has a much smaller magnetic moment of 0.0001 $\mu_B$. The results also indicate that the Gd$_x$Cm$_{1-x}$Sn$_3$ compounds display complex magnetic properties, with a transition from antiferromagnetism to paramagnetism as the Gd concentration increases.

A detailed forecast of beyond standard model particle content is made, taking into account particles that do not interact with photons up to 100 times the mass of a proton. This interaction-free range encompasses many potential beyond standard model candidates, including stable neutrino variants, neutral mesons, and heavy neutral leptons. Organizing potential particles by interaction strength and mass range facilitates research into specific beyond standard model scenarios. This approach is particularly useful for cosmological and astrophysical considerations, as well as for experimental searches at particle accelerators and non-accelerator experiments.

A significant finding by S. Monin and A. Ramet establishes a "foundation theorem" in the context of Coxeter group K-theory. This finding enables multiple distinct approaches to investigate invariants within the Coxeter group ring, specifically for non-reduced Coxeter groups. Utilizing this distinct two-step process, we extend our understanding by generalizing the established findings from A1 and B1 Coxeter group ring generalizations, creating a distinct two-part approach. This process involves first deriving results for B-type Coxeter groups of rank 2, and subsequently applying the "foundation theorem" to derive broader, more complex results.

Gravitational lensing by galaxies offers a powerful method for investigating faint lenses through a phenomenon known as the "boost," which becomes more pronounced with higher supernovae magnitudes. To study this effect, researchers analyzed the Pantheon Type Ia supernovae dataset in conjunction with weak lensing magnification data from 14 independent studies. A significant finding was that supernovae associated with the cosmological component exhibited greater lensing than those linked to host-galaxy bulges or disks, which contradicts the expected behavior based on mass distribution. A possible explanation for this discrepancy is the presence of dark matter halos in the hosts. Furthermore, a comparison with simulations revealed that supernovae located in the outer regions of bulges experience greater gravitational lensing due to a phenomenon called substructure, which includes low-mass satellite galaxies. A notable result was that the lensing effect observed in BCG galaxies was comparable to that observed in BCG clusters.

A new type of photonic structure, called T junction hubs, is presented to overcome limitations of conventional Y junctions in silicon-based integrated optics.  Standard Y junctions suffer from limited branching angles, inefficient 90-degree bends, and excess loss when splitting or combining multiple beams.  In response, a compact T hub with integrated bends and junctions is proposed to streamline photonic circuit design.  By utilizing adiabatic Y junctions and bent waveguides, T hubs achieve low transmission losses of 0.15dB per device across a wide wavelength range from 1520nm to 1580nm.  The T hub's efficiency is further demonstrated through an all-optical 2x4 switch with high crosstalk isolation and balanced power distribution.

Deep contextual object detectors are becoming increasingly important for fully utilizing scene information. To gain a better understanding of how contextual information influences object recognition systems for both straightforward and challenging object detection, we conducted an extensive examination of several leading contextual detectors on the MS COCO dataset. Our study involved ten different base object detectors, four types of context encoders, and various context utilization strategies, with context assessment being performed on scene types and instance relationships as well as on global, regional, and local context.
