For several years, individual sentiment analysis systems have been thoroughly investigated.
However, there is still a lack of cross-lingual sentiment analysis systems capable of
interpreting subjective feelings behind explicit statements in different languages.
This study presents such a model, which leverages translations of foreign language
sentiments to enhance a base local sentiment assessment model.
This study evaluates several methods for utilizing translated data, and finds that
a single model trained on both native and translated sentiment assessment tasks
yields the best results, surpassing the traditional approach of using translated
data to enhance a pre-existing local assessment model.
Additionally, the study's results indicate that a straightforward approach to
utilizing translated annotations leads to significant improvements over standard
methods for assessing sentiment.

This research aims to identify indicators in X-ray images that can help predict which patients with COVID-19 require intensive care unit treatment. It involves using a deep learning model, specifically a ResNet-50, to analyze 108 X-ray images and classify them based on this prediction. The results show that the model can accurately determine ICU admission needs with an area under the curve of 0.85. It also provides a list of features in the X-ray images that are associated with patients requiring intensive care treatment.

The concept of a simplicial bundle was introduced by Whitehead in 1946, and it played a significant role in the development of the Coning Theorem. Over time, various generalizations of this notion have been proposed, and in 1969, Stasheff defined a crucial property known as the simplicial flatness condition. This definition led to the definition of a "simplicial flat map" and subsequently, a "flat simplicial bundle." It was demonstrated that the class of flat simplicial bundles is equivalent to the class of simplicial structures, and this result was achieved by establishing the inclusion of flat simplicial bundles within fibrations, and vice versa. This equivalence was proven by establishing the inclusion of flat simplicial bundles within fibrations, and vice versa.

Positive samples that are incorrectly identified are a significant challenge for deep neural networks, particularly in early stages of training. These erroneous positives can mislead models, causing them to focus on uninformative or incorrect features. Although various techniques have been developed to address difficult negatives, the issue of erroneous positives in visual association detection has received far less attention. In this study, we introduce a new visual association detection task and a corresponding dataset, MMDb-Amazon, built from existing media databases. Based on this, we identify and analyze the elusive yet prevalent erroneous positives in such datasets. A simple yet effective remedy is then proposed to address this issue. Furthermore, a more sophisticated approach is presented that leverages human input to mitigate the impact of these misleading positive samples. Our experiments reveal that 10 to 20% of commonly used positive training data are in fact erroneous positives, and the suggested remedies significantly enhance the performance of visual association detection models.

A galaxy cluster known as Abell 2744, also called El Gordo, presents an intriguing contrast, featuring both well-mixed, well-stirred galaxy components and others that are heavily asymmetrical with significant differences in their outer regions. Our in-depth study of one such asymmetrical part of the El Gordo cluster, focusing on a specific galaxy called EGS-83774, reveals a rich history of interactions with the cluster, revealing that it experienced periods of intense star formation and was influenced by two major events of galaxy interaction. These events contributed to the transfer of inner parts of the galaxy to the cluster, resulting in an accumulation of recently formed star clusters and disrupting the original structure of the galaxy. Notably, despite experiencing significant star formation and structural changes, El Gordo did not undergo a major transformation, retaining its typical characteristics of a relatively undistorted, two-component galaxy with a large bulge and relatively small disk.

On November 7, 2004, a massive solar flare occurred at X4.8 intensity in the sun's north-east quadrant. This event was characterized by multiple radio spikes and gamma radiation, including high-energy neutrons. Observations from space-based detectors revealed a significant number of electron beams with high energy levels, originating from both the north-east and south-west of the solar surface. Observations from ground-based neutron detectors located in the south-west showed an early detection of high-energy neutrons, linked to the south-west location of the detector. These neutrons were generated by a massive proton acceleration event in the south-west solar surface. By analyzing the observed proton energy spectrum and comparing it with previous research, the data revealed a combination of two populations of protons: one with a flat energy distribution and another with a steeper distribution, along with slight time and space differences between the two populations. This research also highlights the importance of considering the geometry of the solar surface and the location of the observer when analyzing solar events, as well as the potential for such events to cause solar storms that can affect Earth's magnetic field and technology.

A recent discovery of a super-Earth, named TOI-1231 b, orbiting very closely to its star presents an unusual situation, as it spins much faster than expected. To explain this, scientists have considered angular momentum transfer, but this theory fails to account for the significant atmospheric escape observed. In contrast, another theory involving angular momentum balance offers a more comprehensive explanation. This theory suggests that TOI 1231 b may be a disintegrating planet, similar to TOI-700 d and Kepler-428 b, with abundant sodium in its atmosphere resulting from the evaporation of rocky debris. However, alternative explanations for the observed absorption lines, such as lines formed within the planet's atmosphere or effects caused by stellar activity, should not be overlooked.

The rapid proliferation of social media has given counterfeit news widespread reach, posing a serious threat to public safety.  Automating the detection of counterfeit news offers a promising solution, but the asymmetrical news data and the lack of available labels present formidable challenges.  Our research focuses on the emergence of multimodal counterfeit news detection using meta neural process networks to automate this task across various platforms using both text and video.  We introduce a novel emergent multi-task learning framework that simultaneously tackles counterfeit news detection in multiple domains while leveraging few-shot data.  We processed over 15 million YouTube news videos to create a large-scale emergent counterfeit news dataset, called Emergent Counterfeit News Dataset (ECND).  Our framework outperforms current methods in single-modal and single-task settings and shows promising results in emergent multi-task settings, even with extremely limited data.  Our results indicate that detecting counterfeit news in new modalities or news types is feasible using our approach.

This research focuses on the occurrence of discontinuities in solutions to a type of transport equation that involves a non-local, time-dependent convolution operator associated with a recurrent probability. A key finding reveals that for certain non-recursive probabilities, specific initial conditions result in persistent discontinuities throughout the equation's solution process. Moreover, the study establishes guidelines outlining the conditions under which these discontinuities are limited to specific points of singularity or can be found at entirely different locations.

This study develops the theoretical framework for GCS, extending previous work on Golay complementary sequences and single-phase signals. GCS consist of three interrelated cophasal signals whose individual pairwise combinations form standard Golay complementary pairs. We explore various design methodologies for both orthogonal and non-orthogonal Golay complementary trees of expanded complexity than their traditional two-design counterparts. A distinctive property of these structures is that second-level branches typically generate four lc pairs per GCP, in contrast to the single GCP produced in conventional Golay trees. However, in cases of non-orthogonal designs, additional b-phase side-branches are necessary to produce the required two GCP per branch, resulting in an overall increased number of Golay pairs in comparison to standard Golay trees. We also examine the practical implications of these polyphase designs for reduced sidelobe patterns in applications such as radar and communications.

Silicon situated in valley splitting regions exhibits enhanced processing capabilities by leveraging its unique physical characteristics. In particular, a novel configuration has been developed on a silicon chip, enabling the transfer of information encoded in quantum states between isolated electrons via the interaction with magnetic impurities. Researchers utilized spatially separated manganese ions and non-equivalent donor sites to examine the influence of long-range valley interaction on spin transfer efficiency between the ions and the donors through the Anti-Symmetrization Effect. By carefully analyzing the relationship between interaction strength and the distance between the ions and the donors, the study found that the transfer efficiency is proportional to the squared distance between them. Furthermore, the investigation revealed that the transfer process is more effective with larger orbital momentum states, offering a potential strategy for controlling long-range interaction in silicon-based technology.

Machine learning techniques, particularly complex models, have excelled in various tasks, yet their internal workings often resemble black boxes with limited interpretability. This limitation poses challenges for applications where understanding the underlying patterns is as important as making accurate predictions, such as in predicting molecular properties or analyzing molecular structures. In this work, we introduce a straightforward approach to uncovering the dynamic and architectural characteristics of intricate system representations learned by advanced graph neural network models. Our method reveals that the learned representations reflect the systems' temporal dependencies and are composed of components that influence both the network's predictive performance and its structural complexity. These insights are objectively verifiable and can be leveraged to enhance network performance and complexity simultaneously. Our findings are supported by analysis of multiple datasets, including synthetic and real-world data, and have been demonstrated in both controlled and natural graph learning environments.

This paper introduces a homotopy-opposite variant of partition games, expanding upon the original game-defined integer sequences from The OEIS. A specific type of standard homotopical partition game is then defined, and both types are demonstrated to generate standard basis elements within their respective monoidal categories. Furthermore, we establish a connection between these types, showing that they are intimately linked through a natural transformation within their respective monoidal categories.

Generating realistic brain lesions in medical images is crucial for improving image segmentation tools and accelerating the acquisition of MRI data. In this study, we developed a new method called PROVAGAN that leverages patient-specific MRI images to create diverse and realistic lesion scenarios automatically. PROVAGAN includes five key components: a patient model to capture the unique image characteristics of each individual, two adversarial components to ensure generated lesions are indistinguishable from real ones and located in the correct image space, and a prior latent variable model to ensure the generated scenarios are diverse. Our method can create diverse, location-inconsistent, and highly realistic brain lesions that are located in image regions suitable for demonstrating disease rather than in high-signal regions, and is capable of generating lesions in images from patients who have no current signs of disease. Our results demonstrate the value of our method for creating training data for image data segmentation and trial data for MRI experiments.

A significant improvement to the GP 2 GenProg input generation compiler was made by Dan Marshall, a PhD candidate at the University of Adelaide. Originally, GP 2 had a basic way to express conditions in expressions, but in a real-world programming context, conditions are frequently used in control flow statements like if, while, and for loops. In this work, Dan developed a more sophisticated method to represent conditions by allowing GP 2 to express conditions in these control flow statements. In experiments with the open-source code of Apache, the corrected 3-run patch success rate improved from 0.105 to 0.111, and in the 2-run scenario, the rate increased from 0.100 to 0.106.

Preprocessing text data often involves extracting specific attributes from sentences, a task that is crucial for many NLP applications. Current research typically addresses this problem by developing separate models for each attribute type, which can be inefficient and cumbersome. In this work, we investigate the issue of attribute extraction for different kinds of attributes, a subset of multi-task learning problems, and we analyze the shared characteristics of attributes found in existing datasets. Our analysis reveals a common structure among attributes, primarily composed of functional and referential components. Building on this insight, we pretrain a Model Unified for Attribute Extraction (MUAE), which selectively identifies and extracts the appropriate component based on the attribute's category. MUAE consists of two contrastive learning branches, each optimized for a different component type. Our MuAE model achieves an F1 score of 85.0, outperforming the second-best current approach which achieves 83.4 when tasked with end-to-end attribute extraction. Furthermore, we make our analysis and MuAE model available to the research community along with the original datasets to facilitate future studies.

This research focuses on developing infinite families of quotient groups from a specific twisted wreath group, denoted as $H_n \wr_\alpha S_{2n}$, where the permutation $\alpha$ has a particular property and the group contains an infinite collection of $S_{2n}$-normal quotients. It is shown that these quotients form a robust, representative set that adheres to a distance metric, providing a useful training dataset for machine learning applications in group theory. Furthermore, we identify 144 distinct representative $S_{2n}$-normal quotient groups within this framework.

For high-dimensional categorical data exploration and modeling, we've developed a novel penalty called the Group L1-p, which is an extension of the L1-p penalty. This penalty is applied to continuous and categorical variables within their respective groups, and we've anced that it leads to variable selection and sparsity across both types of variables. We've incorporated this penalty into generalized linear models and demonstrated its effectiveness through simulations and real-world application to hospital data, which include numerous zero-filled entries. Our method efficiently handles sparse data and has been shown to outperform existing techniques in terms of variable importance, regression performance, and identification of 0-filled variables.

This study introduces a novel structured prediction method to enhance the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) through a modular insight integration framework. Inspired by structured prediction techniques, we developed a new approach called "Structured Insight Infusion" (SKILL) to manage the integration of multiple, diverse, and extensive sources of information. Unlike previous methods, our framework allows for the infusion of completely unconnected, structured modules of knowledge, effectively expanding the parameter space of LLMs. We tested our approach using GPT-3 and found that injecting pre-constructed narrative content from external sources, such as Wikipedia, significantly improved performance on fact-based tasks, with substantial performance gains observed when dealing with extensive, objective content. Our results demonstrate that GPT-3 can seamlessly incorporate complex, objective insights from structured modules, leading to a notable improvement in its performance on fact-based tasks.

As online navigation applications have become increasingly popular, users now expect line representations on vector maps to be rendered precisely, with accurate boundaries and end-points. Although lines on raster maps can be rendered precisely, lines on vector maps often suffer from anti-aliasing effects that blur their borders, end-points, and junctions. These anti-aliasing effects are problematic as they contradict the high precision that users expect from vector maps. While anti-aliasing effects are beneficial in many rendering scenarios, we investigate and address this issue in line representations on vector maps, with the aim of achieving a more precise rendering that meets user expectations. To do this, we develop a efficient spatial anti-aliasing rendering method for line representations on vector maps, with the capacity to effectively eliminate anti-aliasing effects on line boundaries, end-points, and junctions. Our rendering method is highly efficient, with the same time complexity as the original line rendering, with the inclusion of spatial anti-aliasing effects. To validate the efficiency and effectiveness of our approach, we conduct an empirical study that demonstrates the benefits of our algorithm.

To further enhance speech enhancement models based on Apple's High Efficiency Audio Loss, we've developed the Dual Path Convolutional Recurrent Network (DPCRN). This novel architecture integrates a dual-layer design that combines an encoder-decoder module with a recurrent module. Within the encoder-decoder part, dual convolutional paths are employed to retain time-domain information and long-distance dependencies. Then, the recurrent module processes the sequence of time-domain residuals to generate the final speech waveform. Experiments conducted on the LibriSpeech and Switchboard datasets demonstrate the outstanding performance of our model, achieving mean SDR improvements of 3.6 and 2.7 points, respectively, outperforming the top-ranked single-path and multi-domain time-domain methods.

To develop more accurate multi-fluid models of atmospheric processes, it is crucial to first understand single-fluid models. This study focuses on a step in the right direction by creating a single-column simulation of the Rayleigh-Benard convection that includes two fluid models. A step function is used to model atmospheric temperature, which results in upper and lower fluids with distinct thermodynamic properties. A wide range of parameters is explored in 75 large-eddy simulation experiments, and the results reveal the importance of parameter variations on temperature and wind profiles, as well as turbulent heat flux profiles. A subset of 15 experiments with moderate to large Reynolds and Prandtl numbers yields profiles that align with those observed in laboratory settings. By extending previous modeling work, this study paves the way for a more comprehensive understanding of the influence of parameter variations on multi-fluid convection.

A fundamental area of research focuses on distinguishing between entanglement and classical correlations in quantum systems, particularly in systems comprising multiple independent Jaynes-Cummings (JC) interactors. Each interactors consists of a single two-level atom and a specific quantum harmonic oscillator with no photons shared between them. We examine three approaches to create entanglement among the atoms, each starting with atoms in their ground states and harmonic oscillators containing a specific level of excitation. As a result of the nonlinear nature of the state, at least one atom becomes separable from the others in all three approaches. However, our analysis reveals that only one method allows for genuine entanglement among the atoms. We provide a comprehensive understanding of the conditions under which the system exhibits true multi-partite entanglement or even nonlocal correlations, and we map out the associated parameter spaces.

Social media sentiment analysis has become a key area of research due to its
potential applications in various fields. In this study, we focus on analyzing
the emotional content of Twitter messages. We develop an efficient Long Short-Term
Network (LSTM) model for classifying the sentiment of individual tweets. We
utilize a publicly available dataset consisting of 5.1 million tweets to
demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach.

For several decades, researchers have investigated the properties of black holes in anti-de Sitter space by studying shadow charged black holes, which result from the interaction between a Reissner-Nordstrom black hole and a scalar field in higher dimensions. Using Ba\~{n}ados' method, we calculate the quantum correction to the classical shadow radius of these (d+1)-dimensional black holes with charge, and then go on to analyze their thermal behavior by drawing and comparing Smith's and Wilkinsons' contour plots. Our study also involves calculating the quantum corrected temperature and entropy of these black holes with different topological structures. Ultimately, we compare the thermal behaviors observed in our study with those found in previous works that employed different quantum correction methods.

Reconstructing quantum states from tomograms is a widely used technique in quantum state tomography. However, a key issue arises when attempting to solve this task due to the non-linear relationship between the quantum state and its corresponding tomogram. To address this challenge, we propose a method for extracting specific types of state information directly from experimental data. By utilizing Green's functions, we derive two distinct formulas that enable the calculation of a broad range of entanglement measures in multipartite systems, including the concurrence and three-party entanglement measures. We apply this approach to a specific scenario, where a three-qubit system exhibits transition from entanglement to disentanglement and the emergence of classical correlations and synchronization in a specific region of its dynamics. Using this method, we successfully calculate the measures of entanglement and disentanglement directly from experimental data.

360-degree video navigation is an immersive experience that allows viewers to freely explore vast virtual environments. Despite its benefits, network limitations can cause buffering and lag, disrupting the smoothness of the navigation. To address this issue, forecasting the area a viewer will focus on, known as the viewport prediction, is essential. However, existing methods struggle with large-scale, three-dimensional settings. In response to this challenge, we developed a novel method called Subtitle-driven Viewport Forecasting for 360-degree virtual travel video, which utilizes existing subtitle information to forecast the viewer's area of focus. Our Subtitle-driven Viewport Forecasting (SDVF) method consists of two main components: a Subtitle Importance Map (SIM) that identifies the predicted viewport at the current time, and a Subtitle Viewport Transition model (SVT) that anticipates future movements. Our SDVF model excels at forecasting viewer behavior in large-scale, 3D settings, and experimental results demonstrate its superiority over current methods.

Our research develops a localized perspective on non-zero temperature quantum systems within holographic frameworks, leveraging the global/local Schwinger-Keldysh tensor network (SK-SKTN) model. By utilizing SK-SKTN, we gain access to non-perturbative quantum corrections and enhance locality within the dual spacetime, surpassing previous thermal tensor network (TTN) limitations that were confined to the Fefferman-Graham expansion. A significant breakthrough is our ability to derive non-zero temperature Hawking temperatures as well as non-leading 1/ R corrections within the 3D Einstein theory with a negative cosmological constant. Furthermore, we investigate non-equilibrium dynamics in non-compact thermal systems following a sudden quench, leveraging the 1+1+1 SK structure to derive the evolution of thermal systems under temperature changes.

By examining the decoupling phenomenon for functions in Lp spaces on a paraboloid surface, this paper aims to make the recent breakthrough by Bourgain-Bourgain-Guth more accessible and achieve a new improvement. We make three key modifications to their approach to make it more accessible, approximating the decoupling constant using geometric methods, applying Park's approach, and utilizing a simple covering argument to obtain a better estimate. Additionally, this revised approach can be applied to functions defined on a sphere, providing a distinct decoupling approximation.

The color dipole model's fundamental equation, describing the evolution of a gluon within a high-energy hadron at extremely small x values, is known as the Balitsky equation. In the color dipole picture, an important quantity, the impact parameter dependent TMD gluon PDF, plays a key role in describing the interaction of a tiny-angle/tiny-x hadron with a large-$x$ hadron. We've found that the Balitsky equation preserves the power-law, or Bessel-like, structure of the TMD PDF, but also generates new, exponentially growing components that grow as x approaches zero. These components, although theoretically present, are likely unobservable due to being overwhelmed by the power-law components and possibly being subject to unknown non-perturbative corrections that dominate at the smallest x values. Although these non-perturbative corrections are not directly related to renormalalons, their origin and implications remain uncertain. As a result, it's crucial to investigate whether the Balitsky equation can generate non-perturbative, exponentially growing (e.g., $1/x$) TMD PDF components that are attributed to renormalalons. We've found that the Balitsky equation does not generate such components in any impact parameter region, suggesting that the source of these renormalalon-induced components must lie in the Balitsky-Kovchegov TMD PDF initial condition.

Photonic crystals are materials with periodic variations in their refractive index that can be used to control the propagation of light. When a lattice is created on the surface of a 3D photonic crystal, it can give rise to highly directionally concentrated emission or absorption patterns. However, achieving this degree of control requires a highly symmetrical lattice, which is difficult to manufacture. In this study, we found that even lattices with lower levels of symmetry, such as triangular and rectangular shapes, can produce the same degree of surface photonic band edge singularities. We also used the finite-difference time-domain method to investigate a specific type of lattice with oblique symmetry and found it to produce a similar effect. This discovery broadens the range of lattice shapes that can be used to create photonic crystal devices with microscale features that are easier to manufacture.

Decision Support Systems (DSS) assist in making complex choices by considering multiple factors. However, a key challenge lies in obtaining a trained system when a framework is recently decided. Our decision support system handles this issue by transferring knowledge. Previously, we developed a DSS that uses transfer learning to work efficiently with limited data. Now, we're presenting a novel approach by applying black-box knowledge transfer. We treat the black-box decision framework as a no-supply target framework, transferring its learned knowledge even without access to its data. Our method involves a generative model that creates decisions and rewards, enhancing the target framework with synthetic data. We've evaluated our approach in the context of multi-parameter DSS based on the TOPSIS method. Our results show a significant improvement in performance compared to other knowledge transfer approaches, particularly when working with black-box decision frameworks.

We have analyzed the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ decay, obtaining a signal significance of 2.2 sigma and its branching fraction is found to be greater than 1.3 x 10^-6. Additionally, there is an indication for the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} \gamma$ and $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ decays, with their combined combined signal having a significance of 2.6 sigma, and their combined branching fraction is greater than 10^-7.

A significant discovery by Stanley and Brown allows us to apply lattice-building methods from stasys and Adin's work to the lattice of submodules associated with specific modules over group algebras of finite abelian groups. A key aspect of this application involves characterizing submodules through independent sets in a graph defined by a previously established bijection between those modules and elements within an $S_n$-conjugacy class. This bijection was originally found by Burnside. This lattice was first described in its entirety by Michael in 1905. Alternatively, a constructive approach to building this lattice was demonstrated by Dress in 1982 using a morphism from the lattice of subgroups of the symmetric group $S_n$.

In cooperative settings, multiple agents work together to complete a task, 
which can be especially beneficial in complex environments that require too 
much knowledge for a single agent to master.  To work effectively together, 
the ideal Co-Observation Learning scenario would involve each agent having 
access to their own state and those of their peers.  Unfortunately, this 
ideal is rarely feasible in practice due to the difficulty of sharing private 
state information across agents.  This paper presents a Co-Observation Learning 
framework where agents are given second-hand, noisy partial state observations 
of one another, which helps them learn to work effectively together without 
requiring specialized training.  This approach is especially suitable for 
cooperative settings where multiple identical agents work in parallel to 
complete their tasks.  To test the effectiveness of this framework, this paper 
includes several experiments on state-sharing learning, a type of Co-Observation 
Learning that serves as a foundation for a variety of cooperative applications.

In this work, we analyze the anti-aligning code property, a recently discovered phenomenon where codes behave optimally under three types of relationships: superposition, phase, and alignment. These relationships are relevant in quantum phase estimation algorithms and quantum entanglement measurements using parity operators. We investigate two aspects of codes with this property, their mathematical computation and physical measurement, using a generalized least-tossing metric that encompasses previous metrics like Hamming, Jensen-Shannon, and Kullback-Leibler distances. Notable codes with this property include Hadamard and Fourier transform-based codes, as well as new codes specifically designed to minimize this metric, which we demonstrate through both computation and physical experiments using a 12-qubit superconducting quantum processor.

We investigated reinforcement learning techniques to enhance the translation quality produced by our neural machine translation system. To achieve this, we adapted the action space size in our model's training process to an extensive set. The results from multiple trials show that reinforcement learning can yield better outcomes than traditional training methods. The gains in performance are particularly evident in low-resource languages, with rein learning boosting metrics by 0.5 to 1 points. Notably, the Dunje/Ku尔德ish translations benefited the most, with gains of 1 point. To examine the results further, we conducted additional analyses and made our code available online at https://github.com/duygu/rl-nmt-action-space.

In a driven quantum two-level system, a cycle of power absorption and emission occurs, and under specific conditions, the absorbed and emitted power reaches a steady state over time. This non-equilibrium steady state is a distinctive feature of driven two-level systems. This paper presents an in-depth investigation of this phenomenon, utilizing a Rabi cycle drive on a semi-classical diode model. A detailed analysis of the time-dependent current, combined with an impedance diagram, provides insight into the absorbed and emitted power. Notably, at the point of maximum power absorption, the external drive frequency matches the system's intrinsic frequency. In addition to semi-classical analysis, this paper employs a first-order perturbative approach to better understand the absorption and emission processes. This study paves the way for a more comprehensive understanding of the absorption properties of driven quantum two-level systems.

This study focuses on biharmonic hypersurfaces, denoted as $\sigma$-1 or $\sigma$-2, within the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, characterized by recurring properties governed by various operators. Initially, the fundamental concepts of higher-order hypersurfaces, including $k$-mean curvature, $k$-Ricci curvature, and $k$-Sicci curvature, are reviewed. Subsequently, specific equations are examined. For instance, it is proven that any bi-Ricci harmonic hypersurface, denoted as $H$ in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, is necessarily minimal. Moreover, any doubly recurrent bi-Sicci harmonic hypersurface, also denoted as $H$ in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, is shown to be minimal.

A collection of positive integers is said to be $p/q$-identifiable when any infinite sequence that generates the collection as its set of partial sums also produces the collection by taking certain partial sums, specifically those at indices $p, 2q, 3q, \dots$. Previously, it was established that for any $p/q \ge 2$, there exists a $0$-smooth positive $p/q$-identifiable collection. This research enhances that finding by demonstrating the existence of $p/q$-identifiable collections that are $p-1$-smooth.

NoSQL databases, including MongoDB, are gaining popularity for their efficiency with large-scale data. MongoDB's flexible schema and easy replication make it a preferred choice for the backend of content management systems. However, the lack of transactional support in MongoDB's primary/secondary replication model poses a risk of data corruption in the event of system failures. This research presents a new framework for ensuring transactional data consistency in MongoDB's primary/secondary replication model. By creating transactional hashes for collections and verifying them during replication, the proposed solution ensures that transactions remain consistent and prevents potential data corruption. The effectiveness of this solution is demonstrated through a case study involving the backend of Wikipedia's mobile application.

A combinatorial method has been developed to positively break down the chromatic symmetric polynomials into elementary Schur functions positively. This is due to a newly discovered property of the Schur function coefficients of which an $e$-positivity pattern is observed. The combinatorial meaning of this $e$-positivity is also established through an inverse combinatorial rule known as the inverse Kostka tableau, which reinterprets the non-negative coefficients in the chromatic symmetric polynomials' expansion in terms of the monomial basis.

A study focusing on a concealed geometric structure within a specific type of
nanoscale assembly, where triangles formed by adjacent atoms dictate the
arrangement of the assembly. This assembly, consisting of triangular and
hexagonal nanoscale elements made of cobalt atoms, was used to investigate
geometric frustration within a system exhibiting triangle-based frustation. By
analyzing how the assembly's geometry influenced magnetic ordering patterns,
researchers found that the system with only triangle elements served as a base
geometry for describing the system with triangle and hexagon elements. This
description led to the identification of three distinct magnetic phases,
including one with unusual spiral ordering. Experimental and simulation data
were found to be in close agreement.

Recent observations from the Parker Solar Probe (PSP) have allowed for a visualization of the solar breeze in the inner solar system, providing valuable data for analyzing the energy transfer mechanisms of the solar wind. Using the solar wind velocity profiles recorded by the FIELDS instrument at 18-20 solar radii, we have developed a model to predict the energy transfer processes, accounting for wave and turbulence influences. The model reveals that Alfv\'enic turbulence is the primary contributor to heating, with residual energy likely absorbed by ion cyclotron resonance. As the solar wind travels through space, residual energy is thought to be lost as heat, while Alfv\'enic resonance continues to drive heating processes. These findings are particularly significant given the inner solar system observation context of PSP and contribute to our comprehension of the coronal problem.

A speech-emotion recognition system is a fundamental human-computer interaction technology. Nevertheless, it still encounters significant challenges, particularly due to the frequent domain dependency and lack of emotional expressions in most speech-emotion recognition datasets. We investigate two difficult and interconnected problems: domain adaptation and emotion recognition from speech for a dataset that includes both diverse speakers and multiple domains. In addressing these challenges, we first focus on a particular difficult scenario where the target domain data is scarce. By leveraging source domains, we adapt a speech-emotion recognition model that has been pre-trained using a universal dataset, Melt. We employ a distinctive approach by exploiting the spectral features of speech, which exhibit robustness across different domains, to adapt the model in the frequency domain. We evaluate our method on the CREMA-D and IEMOCAP datasets, demonstrating notable performance improvements over existing adaptation techniques.

We investigate the impact of a localized shock wave that propagates through an expanding universe, specifically focusing on a model with a spherical void at its center. A perfect fluid is considered, and we derive analytical solutions for an adiabatic process, as well as solutions for an isothermal process. Our research indicates that the interactions between the shock wave and the expansion of the universe can lead to the overcompression and overheating of matter, potentially resulting in star formation within a previously underdense region.

Utilizing the LHCb experiment data, a study was conducted on the form of the $B_s^0\rightarrow D_s^{*-}\mu^{+}\nu_{\mu}$ differential decay rate. A form based on four parameters was employed to analyze this differential decay rate, revealing clear evidence for $D_s^{*-}$ production in this process with a significance of 10.1 sigma. Furthermore, initial estimates of the form factors at zero recoil were obtained, yielding values of $0.002\pm 0.011\pm 0.003$ for $f_3(0)$ and $-0.002\pm 0.011\pm 0.003$ for $f_4(0)$.

A recent study classifies Schrödinger operators with rational potentials that have specific growth properties at infinity with no unique continuous spectrum. Such operators have polynomial solutions to their eigenvalue equations. An in-depth examination links an algebraic characteristic of these polynomial solutions, having no common factors, to the operators' Hecke-like properties. This connection facilitates the derivation of an explicit general form for the potential functions based on a comprehensive class of polynomial sequences. This class encompasses various polynomial sequences, including Hermite, Bessel, and Airy, among others.

When an adhesive tape or strip is peeled off a surface, the sound produced can be quite loud and unpredictable, a phenomenon known as the "crackling effect." This research investigates the hidden patterns behind the sound spectrum generated during this process. By applying a spectral analysis to recorded sound data, we discovered evidence of specific, consistent frequency patterns in the "crackling effect" across multiple instances of peeling an adhesive strip. The situation is comparable to studying the vibration patterns of a drumhead, and further investigation reveals that these patterns correspond to the vibrations of the strip as it bends, a phenomenon referred to as the "snap." Moreover, several variables, including the size of the strip, its width, its stiffness, and its speed of peeling, impact the sound's frequency pattern.

In the context of a non-abelian gauge theory coupled to a "aether-like" non-hermitian non-abelian gauge field term, a thermal temperature exists above which a non-abelian aether-like term becomes positive. This positive term results in the spontaneous formation of a non-abelian aether-like field at finite temperature and zero chemical potential, leading to the emergence of new effective non-abelian gauge field masses. These masses are calculated in the thermal range and expressed in terms of the "aether-like" field magnitude and the temperature.

We examine the pricing of options priced with dynamic delta hedging and refer to the resulting price as the collateral option. By leveraging stochastic hedging techniques, our model derives the European option's price with a hedging error of zero, utilizing the underlying asset as collateral and accounting for interest expenses at a specific rate. Furthermore, our model provides insight into how the option behaves when the underlying rate is constant or linearly dependent on time.

A mathematical model of intergenerational mobility is given an economic basis, revealing that an individual's opportunity structure consists of two key components: social mobility and social prospects. Social mobility refers to the probability distribution of an individual's future status based on their current and parental status, while social prospects represent the probability distribution of future statuses independent of current and parental status. In dynamic frameworks, the social prospects component exhibits convexity or concavity depending on the desirability of extreme statuses. A social prospects framework influences optimal policy and market prospects by affecting the status of individuals with high parental socioeconomic status. Specifically, it leads to the accumulation of individuals with high socioeconomic status, prompting social welfare maximization through mobility enhancement rather than status accumulation. The research indicates that the social prospects component drives the accumulation of extreme socioeconomic statuses at both ends of the status spectrum.

This presentation delves into the utilization of brightness scans for beam diagnostics, a technique that has proven effective in diagnosing beam issues at facilities like MAX IV and DESY. A brightness scan involves gradually altering a specific beam parameter, such as aperture size, emittance, or beta function, and monitoring the corresponding change in beam brightness. This method's success relies on the beam brightness responding predictably to a log-scale parameter change, a relationship that can be exploited to diagnose issues using tools like fits and differentials. Although initially applied to transverse beam analysis, this technique's potential is far-reaching, with applications in analyzing both transverse and longitudinal beams.

The development of resource-intensive iterative algorithms for machine learning has been facilitated by distributed algorithms that leverage data from multiple devices. However, these algorithms can be hindered by malicious nodes that manipulate the outcome by injecting false information. This research has explored the creation of robust, Malicious Assault-Resistant Improvement Technique (MART) algorithms that are feasible for implementation in a distributed environment. MART algorithms guarantee convergence to an optimal solution that is comparable to that of a singular, centralized algorithm. This research has provided analytical and verifiable convergence rates for two variations of MART algorithms under different rates of Malicious Assault injection. The Martingale technique has been utilized to analyze the rate of convergence. Furthermore, the application of MART algorithms has been demonstrated through results from a Malicious Assault experiment on logistic regression.

The s4cmb package enables the simulation of instrumental patterns for the
Cosmic Microwave Background due to the movement of instruments. To accurately
replicate real-world conditions, it's crucial to model the instrumentation's
effects, including coordinate system conversions, conversion of temperature
fluctuations to the focal plane, and the movement of instruments across the sky.
This paper presents the calculation method and a practical implementation using
Python for these models. To demonstrate its application, we used the s4cmb package
to model the data collected by the SPT-3G camera and the South Pole Telescope.

Research into deep language understanding has been significantly advanced by
pre-trained linguistic models, yet their specific role in tasks involving complex
language usage remains unclear. This study investigates whether these models
have internalized the rules of intricate language phenomena by examining their
performance on syntactically challenging tasks, specifically word arrangement. We
found that the BART model excels at reconstructing sentences from scrambled
words, outperforming models previously developed to address this challenge.
However, this success may not reflect true word arrangement capability, as the BART
model appears to achieve high performance by leveraging robust contextual
understanding rather than a deep grasp of syntactic structures. This hypothesis
is confirmed by experiments using models without contextual cues, which showed a
decline in performance comparable to the drop in input cues. These findings have
important implications for a deeper exploration of the complex language
understanding exhibited by pre-trained models.

For the escalating issue of multimedia misinformation caused by deepfake technology, there is an urgent need to develop more effective detection methods. Deepfake generation models introduce novel artifacts that are minute and often evade conventional frequency-based detection techniques. In reality, digital images and videos contain structure and semantics at various scales, from local patterns to high-level meanings, that play a crucial role in perceptual authenticity. In response to this challenge, we propose a novel frequency- and semantics-aware detection method called the MD-CSDNetwork, which combines multi-scale feature extraction from a backbones' intermediate layers, style information from convolution operations, and semantics from attention mechanisms. Our proposed network integrates these elements through a carefully designed architecture comprising an attention-based global semantic module and a cross sewn multi-scale and style fusion module. Through extensive experiments on prominent deepfake detection datasets, our method consistently demonstrates superior performance, outperforming state-of-the-art techniques in accuracy, along with additional analyses that highlight its robustness across different attack methods, generalization capabilities, and style transfer resistance.

In 1930, Menger developed a concept of distance-based angles within general metric spaces, and subsequently, he identified two metric spaces where distances beyond zero are defined, but these angles remain undefined or unmeaningful. Menger regarded these issues as theoretical problems and did not incorporate them into the axiomatic structure of his metric space distance angle concept. However, he did not address these issues before or after presenting his work. Now, the paper at hand demonstrates that the previously undefined angles correspond to four-point stars and 120-degree triangle configurations, and by further research, it is possible to define a consistent distance-based angle that matches the initial configurations for all specified points and combinations. Moreover, the paper shows that this distance-based angle definition aligns with an existing axiomatic framework for absolute value and scalar field order relationships.

In this work, a bound is established on the difference between consecutive sorted prime number coefficients of certain Eulerian polynomials, denoted as $p_n/x$, where these coefficients correspond to the counts of permutations with $n$-elements in their largest possible cycles. Specifically, the difference between any two adjacent coefficients is less than $4^n-1$. This result has significant implications for a longstanding unproven conjecture by Edixhoven regarding the prime number coefficients of Hilbert polynomials, $P_n(\cdot)$, associated with $\GL_n$ orbits within $\mathbb{Z}^n\!\sube{+}$, suggesting that the difference between any two adjacent coefficients, $P_n(x_j)$ and $P_n(x_{j+1})$, is also less than $4^n-1$.

This paper provides a detailed cluster algebraic characterization of positive parts of nilpotent Lie algebras under the Kac-Vergne classification. Building upon the work of Feletti and Negri, we achieve this by formulating explicit mutation rules for a specific class of geometric representations. These representations serve as starting points for the Grassmannian of dimension $2p$ in $\mathbb{C}^{2n}$, nilpotent subalgebras of $\mathfrak{sl}_n(\mathbb{C})$, and the space of skew-symmetric forms. Through these representations, we prove that the Preyelsky-Bergman basis, which is fundamental to the Kac-Vergne construction, exhibits a strong cluster algebraic property. Additionally, we establish the strong cluster algebraic nature of the Grassmannian, Nilvarieties, and Ovarieties.

Forsage, which peaked at a $310 million referral fee in 2020 before being shut down, was an elaborate multi-level marketing scheme based on blockchain technology. Due to the lack of research into pyramid schemes from this technological perspective, we analyzed Forsage's code to better understand its intricate structure. Our examination reveals a complex pyramid scheme, with user interactions and blockchain technology integrated into its design. Unlike traditional MLM schemes, Forsage utilized cryptographic hash functions to create unique identifiers for users and organized them into constantly changing hierarchical clusters. Our findings are of interest to computer scientists studying social networks and blockchain technology, as well as to policymakers and legal professionals dealing with MLM fraud. To facilitate this, we made the source code for Forsage publicly available on GitHub.

A VVV survey vector has been created to investigate the structure of globular clusters in the Milky Way galaxy. By analyzing VVV survey images, researchers can re-examine established globular cluster classifications and identify previously unrecognized groups. This study re-evaluates globular clusters located within globular cluster databases and searches for new clusters within a specific view volume. VVV survey images are particularly suited for identifying clusters in view volume regions that were previously under-sampled. This investigation has re-evaluates 19 candidate clusters by examining their color-opacity diagrams, light curves, and stellar population parameters. This analysis has confirmed the veracity of some candidate clusters and compared their characteristics to well-studied globular clusters. By continuing to monitor the VVV survey volume, researchers can confirm the status of 25 previously unconfirmed clusters that were identified during this investigation. In order to investigate and simulate complex adaptive systems with intricate interactions, holographic models offer an effective tool. A key feature of these models is their ability to model models of complex systems that exhibit intricate, non-trivial behaviors. Our research introduces an improved version of the holographic model known as the hyper-invariant MERA, which is particularly well-suited for models of complex systems with intricate, non-trivial dynamics. The framework of holographic models also provides a unique perspective on information management in complex systems by likening their dynamics to a form of error correction. In this context, our new hologeric model is found to be comparable to previously developed error correction techniques, which utilize a unique, logarithmic-based approach to manage information fidelity across different scales. Our research reveals that the hlogarithmic approach is the most efficient and optimal method for managing information in systems with intricate, non-trivial interactions. Our study also explores alternative, non-trivial approaches to 2D complex systems that utilize the hologeric model and its associated tools.

The explosive growth of big data has fueled the rapid development of machine learning, with neural networks in particular experiencing significant advancements. These technologies have been applied to a wide range of fields, including the analysis and prediction of business processes (BPs). The intricate and vast nature of business processes poses substantial challenges for prediction, prompting the need for innovative approaches. This study introduces a cutting-edge BP forecasting framework, leveraging pattern recognition and classification using machine learning and time-series forecasting via artificial neural networks. The proposed framework is tested on the well-known German Credit Card customer service process dataset, yielding superior forecasting results compared to existing methods. The excellent performance of this approach is demonstrated, providing a robust and efficient solution for predicting business processes.

We establish that Gelfand-Shilov spaces can be characterized through their rapid decrease in Fourier transforms, thereby demonstrating their non-compact support in both time and frequency domains. Furthermore, this approach enables us to prove that the domains of certain Toeplitzians are not extension-closed, specifically for symbols that are smooth and rapidly decreasing in both time and frequency domains.

Carbuncles, which are persistent structures found in sunspots, have long fascinated astronomers. Researchers have tried to recreate a massive solar eruption, in this case involving the red dwarf star, named AD Leonis, during its 1985 huge event. By combining observational data from various sources, scientists developed a 3D model of this eruption's UV radiation. The eruption was so powerful that it exceeded the star's magnetic field capacity, resulting in a massive C-class solar flare and a huge coronal hole. The simulation accurately replicated the spectral features seen in observations, including the green line and H-alpha absorption patterns. The simulation also showed that the eruption's electron flux was capable of inducing a significant geomagnetic storm on Earth.

3D object recognition tasks require robust smoothening of point cloud data to prevent overfitting and reduce noise. Traditional data augmentation techniques provide a basic level of smoothing, but more advanced methods are necessary. Our proposed dynamic smoothing framework adaptively applies a variable-degree Gaussian filter to point clouds, mimicking natural variations in object representations found in the wild. Experimental results demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms traditional augmentation techniques on multiple benchmarks, including object detection with Moderate-to-Difficult Amplitude Transformations (MODAT) achieving 36.6 mAP and point cloud classification with PointNet, yielding 79.0 classification accuracy. Our code is available at this GitHub repository: https://github.com/andrewswenson/tpc.

This formulation enables the RPA R-matrix spectral function to be visually represented.
